questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My family is living in Sydney

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, The University of Sydney has been very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails, and a good possibility to reach out if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficuilt to fin housing outside campus, but it became much easier when we were here. I feel fortunate that we found a good place in Surry Hills, but if I had been alone, I would have chosen the options on campus. But because I before I arrived found some other exchange students who also were looking for an apartment, we were more people to look and managed to find a hole apartment together. I think that was much nicer, but the market is horrible, and it is really easy to be scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Patience, if you want to find housing off campus, but if you feel that it will be too stressful not having anything when you arrive, then just choose the campus options - they are not that more expensive than the options you can find off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very expensive on campus when thinking about how you share everything with others.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If was very easy, because we did it online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: both online and help on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100 pct. successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seems like everybody got the courses they wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a bit easier than my university, but I still think that it was academically challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar to holdundervisning at kernefaglig on statskundskab

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chinese Politics, Enviromental Politics, Gender, Security and Human Rights and US-China relations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Chinese Politics (very interesting seeing the Chinese case from an Australian-China perspective), Environmental Politics (the kindest professor ever), Gender, Security and Human Rights (very qualified professors)

questions.answer: none - but a lot of travelling.

questions.answer: Food was cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were plenty of options, way more than at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty of clubs, swimming pool etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the possibilities you have at hand - join the clubs, meet people. Join the USU - they give free food all the time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tasmania and New Zealand as well as Whitsundays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture is very similar to ours, just a bit more coffee spots.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to those in your class, because they are not in the uni clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Finding so many new friends, enjoying the weather, try a real campus experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Decide before going what to do with housing so you don't get stressed. Are you willing to take the risk of not having a place to stay for the first couple of months. Say YES to things! Use every opportunity to go out and see stuff - even though it is with people that you do not know especially well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new friends, being a part of a new culture, just taking interesting electives, being a part of a on campus life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being so far from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
